recentItems.title: Moveable Feast: Gronk in Conversation with Paul Holdengräber
recentItems.description:
Moveable Feast continues to explore Los Angeles arts and culture with a special presentation featuring renowned visual and performance artist Gronk in conversation with Paul Holdengräber.

In a far-ranging conversation, Holdengräber and Gronk dive into the artist's younger years, when he was part of the famed avant-garde multimedia arts collective known as Asco; together they examine his numerous collaborations with stage designers, directors and musicians. 

In partnership with USC and supported by Mei-Lee Ney and Selma Holo, Moveable Feast brings together arts partners and creative voices to shape collective experiences. Each conversation is a journey, where ideas travel and evolve to deepen our understanding of the world and ourselves.

As mentioned during the conversation, see some of Gronk’s daily drawings on Instagram @elgronk

Learn more about this event at https://www.caltech.edu/campus-life-events/calendar/moveable-feast-gronk-in-conversation-with-paul-holdengraber

recentItems.title: Geological and Biological Processes at the Zaonega Formation 2 Billion Years Ago
recentItems.description:
According to a recent study led by Caltech researchers, the interplay of local geological and biological processes illustrated in the video can fully account for the unusual carbon-isotope signal recorded in rocks of the Zaonega Formation, which has often been interpreted as evidence of a global carbon cycle change.
Learn more at https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/new-info-from-ancient-rocks-upends-popular-theory.

recentItems.title: mITRAR: Expanding First Responder Capabilities Through AI, Coordination, and Decision Support
recentItems.description:
In January 2025, unprecedented fires burned through communities across Los Angeles County.

In the months that followed, Caltech scientists and engineers developed new technologies to expand first responder capabilities through intelligent systems, coordination, and decision support.

Learn more about Caltech's Center for Autonomous Systems and Technologies (CAST): https://cast.caltech.edu
